title: Running Median
statement:
Integers arrive one at a time. After each arrival, report the **median** of all integers received so far. When the count is even there are two middle values; report the **smaller** one.

**Input.** The first line holds `n`; the second holds the `n` integers in order of arrival.

**Output.** `n` medians, one after each arrival, separated by spaces on one line.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 20000 in this browser version (the idea scales to 10^6)
hints: Keeping a sorted array and inserting each value costs O(n) per insertion because of the shifting. Can you avoid keeping everything sorted?
The median only needs the largest value of the smaller half and the smallest value of the larger half. Keep the smaller half in a max-heap and the larger half in a min-heap.
Insert the new value into the correct half, then rebalance so the smaller half has the same number of values as the larger half, or one more. The median is the top of the smaller half.
editorial: Split the values seen so far into a **lower half** and an **upper half** such that every value of the lower half is at most every value of the upper half, and the lower half holds `ceil(count / 2)` values. Then the (lower) median is the **maximum of the lower half**. A max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half expose exactly the two boundary values in O(1). For a new value `x`: if it is larger than the lower half's maximum it belongs to the upper half, otherwise to the lower half. Then rebalance with at most one move: if the lower half has more than one extra value, move its maximum to the upper half; if the upper half is larger, move its minimum to the lower half. Each arrival costs `O(log n)`, so the total is `O(n log n)`, against `O(n^2)` for insertion into a sorted array. Python's heapq is a min-heap only, so negate the values of the lower half; JavaScript needs a hand-written heap.

starter.python:
import sys
import heapq

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
# the n integers are data[1], data[2], ..., data[n]

solutions.python:
import sys
import heapq

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
low, high = [], []          # low: the smaller half as a max-heap (values negated); high: the larger half as a min-heap
out = []
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    x = int(data[i])
    if low and x > -low[0]:
        heapq.heappush(high, x)
    else:
        heapq.heappush(low, -x)
    if len(low) > len(high) + 1:              # keep len(low) equal to len(high) or one more
        heapq.heappush(high, -heapq.heappop(low))
    elif len(high) > len(low):
        heapq.heappush(low, -heapq.heappop(high))
    out.append(-low[0])                       # the largest of the smaller half is the (lower) median
print(" ".join(map(str, out)))
